Gold's loss widened to 2.0 percent at 4,066.9 from 4,097.3 and a 1.27 percent loss, silver's loss widened to 3.55 percent at 55.38 from 55.85 and a 2.75 percent loss, and oil eased to a 1.95 percent gain at 99.04 from a 2.54 percent gain at 99.62. The equity pipe is the cash price of listed-stock indexes, so the lower S&P and Nasdaq prints mean the cash value of those indexes fell, the metals pipe is the cash price of gold and silver, so the wider losses mean the cash value of metals fell, and the oil pipe is the cash price of crude, which is still higher on the day.
